title: Blind Bartimaeus
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow (1807-1882)
lyricSources: the original lyrics by Longfellow retained the Greek quotes of the New Testament for the "three voices".  Published in "Ballads and other poems, 1842.  English translations of the Greek were added later by an unknown translator before the above lyric source.
verses: He hears the crowd; he hears a breath
And calls in tones of agony,
But still, above the noisy crowd,
The blind man's cry is shrill and loud:
Then saith the Christ, as silent stands
The crowd, "What wilt thou at My hands?"
And he replies, "O give me light!
Rabbi, restore the blind man's sight."
Thy faith, thy faith hath savèd thee."
Ye that hath eyes and cannot see,
"Thy faith, thy faith hath savèd thee."
